title.hanzi: 那个唱歌的女孩子是谁？
title.pinyin: Nàge chàng gē de nǚháizi shì shéi?

instruction.hanzi: 读一读，说说这些词语是什么意思。
instruction.english: Read the words and phrases aloud and say what they mean.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 王明，那个唱歌的女孩子是谁？
dialogue.pinyin: Wáng Míng, nàge chàng gē de nǚ háizi shì shéi?
dialogue.english: Wang Ming, who's the girl singing over there?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 她是我的同学，也姓王。
dialogue.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de tóngxué, yě xìng Wáng.
dialogue.english: She's my classmate. Her surname is Wang too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 她唱的歌真好听！
dialogue.pinyin: Tā chàng de gē zhēn hǎotīng!
dialogue.english: The song she's singing sounds great!

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 是啊，她每天都唱歌。
dialogue.pinyin: Shì a, tā měi tiān dōu chàng gē.
dialogue.english: Yes, she sings every day.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 她右边的那个男孩子呢？
dialogue.pinyin: Tā yòubian de nàge nán háizi ne?
dialogue.english: And the boy on her right?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 那是她男朋友，也是我们学校的学生。
dialogue.pinyin: Nà shì tā nán péngyou, yě shì wǒmen xuéxiào de xuésheng.
dialogue.english: That's her boyfriend. He's a student at our school too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 你好，这件衣服多少钱？
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, zhè jiàn yīfu duōshao qián?
dialogue.english: Hi, how much is this jacket?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.pinyin: Sānbǎi bāshí kuài.
dialogue.english: Three hundred and eighty kuai.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 太贵了。有便宜一点儿的吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Tài guì le. Yǒu piányi yìdiǎnr de ma?
dialogue.english: That's too expensive. Do you have anything a bit cheaper?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 你看看右边这件，这件比那件便宜100块。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ kànkan yòubian zhè jiàn, zhè jiàn bǐ nà jiàn piányi yìbǎi kuài.
dialogue.english: Have a look at this one on the right. It's a hundred kuai cheaper than that one.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 颜色也很漂亮。我能试一下吗？
dialogue.pinyin: Yánsè yě hěn piàoliang. Wǒ néng shì yíxià ma?
dialogue.english: The color is nice too. Can I try it on?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 可以，请到这边来。
dialogue.pinyin: Kěyǐ, qǐng dào zhèbian lái.
dialogue.english: Sure, come this way please.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 九点了，刘老师怎么还没来？
dialogue.pinyin: Jiǔ diǎn le, Liú lǎoshī zěnme hái méi lái?
dialogue.english: It's nine o'clock. Why isn't Professor Liu here yet?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 她可能生病了。
dialogue.pinyin: Tā kěnéng shēng bìng le.
dialogue.english: Maybe she's ill.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 不会吧？昨天她还很好呢。
dialogue.pinyin: Bú huì ba? Zuótiān tā hái hěn hǎo ne.
dialogue.english: Surely not? She was perfectly fine yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 那可能是路上车太多了。
dialogue.pinyin: Nà kěnéng shì lù shang chē tài duō le.
dialogue.english: Then maybe there's too much traffic on the road.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 你听，有人来了。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ tīng, yǒu rén lái le.
dialogue.english: Listen, someone's coming.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 是刘老师！我们别说话了。
dialogue.pinyin: Shì Liú lǎoshī! Wǒmen bié shuō huà le.
dialogue.english: It's Professor Liu! Let's stop talking.

title.english: Wang Ming talks about his brother

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 我有一个哥哥，他比我大三岁，也比我高一点儿。
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí ge gēge, tā bǐ wǒ dà sān suì, yě bǐ wǒ gāo yìdiǎnr.
dialogue.english: I have an older brother. He's three years older than me and a little taller, too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 去年他开始工作了。
dialogue.pinyin: Qùnián tā kāishǐ gōngzuò le.
dialogue.english: He started working last year.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 他的工作很忙，可是每个星期六都回家看爸爸妈妈。
dialogue.pinyin: Tā de gōngzuò hěn máng, kěshì měi ge xīngqīliù dōu huí jiā kàn bàba māma.
dialogue.english: His job keeps him very busy, but he comes home every Saturday to see our parents.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 哥哥很爱说话，我不太爱说话。
dialogue.pinyin: Gēge hěn ài shuō huà, wǒ bú tài ài shuō huà.
dialogue.english: My brother loves to talk; I'm not much of a talker.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 他明年可能会来北京看我。
dialogue.pinyin: Tā míngnián kěnéng huì lái Běijīng kàn wǒ.
dialogue.english: He might come to Beijing to visit me next year.

title.english: A Verb Phrase + 的 Describing a Noun

explanation.hanzi: 动词或动词短语后面加"的"，可以放在名词前面，说明是哪个人或者哪个东西。这和英语的定语从句（the person who…, the clothes that…）意思一样，可是中文的顺序是：说明在前，名词在后。
explanation.english: To say which person or thing you mean, put a verb phrase + 的 in front of the noun. It does the job of an English relative clause ("the person who...", "the clothes that..."), but the order is reversed: the description comes first and the noun comes last. 唱歌的那个人 = "the person who is singing"; 我昨天买的衣服 = "the clothes I bought yesterday". If the noun is clear from context, it can be left out: 坐在右边的是马克 "The one sitting on the right is Mark."

examples.hanzi: 唱歌的那个人是我的同学。
examples.pinyin: Chàng gē de nàge rén shì wǒ de tóngxué.
examples.english: The person singing is my classmate.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天买的衣服很便宜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān mǎi de yīfu hěn piányi.
examples.english: The clothes I bought yesterday were very cheap.

examples.hanzi: 刘老师说的话我都听懂了。
examples.pinyin: Liú lǎoshī shuō de huà wǒ dōu tīngdǒng le.
examples.english: I understood everything Professor Liu said.

examples.pinyin: Zuò zài yòubian de shì Mǎkè.
examples.english: The one sitting on the right is Mark.

explanation.hanzi: "A 比 B + 形容词"表示 A 和 B 比，A 怎么样。形容词前面不能用"很"、"非常"。要说出差多少，就把数量放在形容词后面："他比我大三岁"、"这件比那件便宜一百块"、"马克比王明高一点儿"。
explanation.english: "A 比 B + adjective" means "A is more [adjective] than B". Do not put 很 or 非常 before the adjective: say 今天比昨天热, not 今天比昨天很热. To say by how much, put the amount after the adjective: 他比我大三岁 "He is three years older than me", 这件比那件便宜一百块 "This one is 100 kuai cheaper than that one". 一点儿 after the adjective means "a little".

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gēge bǐ wǒ dà sān suì.
examples.english: My older brother is three years older than me.

examples.hanzi: 这个西瓜比那个便宜五块。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xīguā bǐ nàge piányi wǔ kuài.
examples.english: This watermelon is five kuai cheaper than that one.

examples.pinyin: Mǎkè bǐ Wáng Míng gāo yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: Mark is a bit taller than Wang Ming.

explanation.hanzi: "可能"放在动词或形容词前面，表示说话人估计、猜测某件事，不是很确定。否定形式是"可能不……"或"可能没……"。"可能"后面常常加"会"。回答问题的时候，也可以只说"可能"。
explanation.english: 可能 (kěnéng) goes before a verb or adjective to make a guess: "may, might, probably". The speaker isn't sure. The negative is 可能不 + verb ("might not") or 可能没 + verb ("probably didn't"). It often combines with 会: 他可能会来 "He might come". On its own, 可能 can answer a question: "Maybe."

examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān kěnéng bù lái le.

examples.hanzi: 你明年还来北京吗？——可能。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ míngnián hái lái Běijīng ma? — Kěnéng.
examples.english: Are you coming back to Beijing next year? — Maybe.

prompt.hanzi: 两人一组，分角色读课文。
prompt.english: In pairs, read the dialogues aloud, taking one role each.

prompt.hanzi: 根据你的情况回答问题。

items.hanzi: 你比你的好朋友大吗？大几岁？
items.pinyin: Nǐ bǐ nǐ de hǎo péngyou dà ma? Dà jǐ suì?
items.english: Are you older than your best friend? By how many years?
Where did you go last year?

items.pinyin: Míngtiān kěnéng huì xià yǔ ma?

prompt.hanzi: 用"比、可能、姓、的、便宜"填空。
prompt.english: Fill in the blanks with 比, 可能, 姓, 的 or 便宜.

items.english: My older brother is five years older than me.

items.hanzi: 王明今天没来，他____生病了。
items.english: Wang Ming didn't come today; maybe he's ill.

items.hanzi: 坐在右边____那个男孩子是马克。
items.english: The boy sitting on the right is Mark.

items.hanzi: 这个杯子很____，十块钱一个。
items.english: These cups are very cheap, ten kuai each.

prompt.hanzi: 给问题找到合适的回答。
prompt.english: Match each question with a suitable answer.

items.pinyin: Nín xìng shénme? — Wǒ xìng Wáng.
items.english: What is your surname? — My surname is Wang.

items.hanzi: 唱歌的那个人是谁？ — 是我的同学。
items.pinyin: Chàng gē de nàge rén shì shéi? — Shì wǒ de tóngxué.
items.english: Who is the person singing? — My classmate.

items.hanzi: 哪件便宜？ — 右边这件。
items.pinyin: Nǎ jiàn piányi? — Yòubian zhè jiàn.
items.english: Which one is cheaper? — This one on the right.

items.hanzi: 他今天会来吗？ — 可能不来了。
items.pinyin: Tā jīntiān huì lái ma? — Kěnéng bù lái le.
items.english: Is he coming today? — Probably not.

singleComponentChars.etymology: Two people standing side by side, facing the same way. Putting two things next to each other is how you compare them.

radicals.english: woman (related to women, family and names)
mouth (related to speaking, eating and sounds)

prompt.hanzi: 两人一组或几人一组，比一比，说一说。
prompt.english: In pairs or small groups, compare things and describe people.

activities: Who's who: look around the classroom (or at a photo) and describe people with verb phrase + 的: 坐在右边的…, 正在说话的…, 穿红衣服的…. Your partner guesses who it is.
Family comparisons: tell your partner about a brother, sister or friend using 比: 他比我大……岁, 她比我高一点儿.
Shopping: compare two items in a shop with 这件比那件便宜/贵……块 and decide which one to buy.
Guessing game: your partner names a classmate who is absent today; give reasons with 可能: 他可能生病了 / 他可能在睡觉.
